title: "Workers AI"

---

Cloudflare's own models, run in the same Cloudflare account as your Gateway. There's no separate sign-up and nothing to prepay: usage is billed to that account.

**Used by:** [Agentic Inbox](/docs/apps/agentic-inbox) can use it as its model provider.

## API key

- **Get your key here:** [dash.cloudflare.com](https://dash.cloudflare.com/profile/api-tokens)
- **Setting:** `WORKERS_AI_API_TOKEN`
- **API reference:** [developers.cloudflare.com](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/)

### Get the key

1. In the Cloudflare dashboard, open the [Workers AI page](https://dash.cloudflare.com/?to=/:account/ai/workers-ai) of your Gateway's account.
2. Select **Use REST API**, then **Create a Workers AI API Token**. The form comes prefilled with Workers AI permissions on this account; check the account and select **Create API Token**.
3. Copy the token. It's shown once.
4. `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` is your Gateway's own account, which `everyapp setup` already set. You only set the token.

### Set it on your Gateway

From your EveryApp folder:

```bash
pnpm everyapp secret set WORKERS_AI_API_TOKEN
```

It asks for the value at a hidden prompt, and it's live at once, with no deploy. If an app you've installed needs it, `pnpm everyapp configure <app>` asks for it along with everything else the app needs.

To make it the model provider apps get when they ask for the default:

```bash
pnpm everyapp ai default workers-ai
```

### Use it in an app

List it in the app's `everyapp.config.ts`:

```ts
providers: ["workers-ai"],
```

The app calls `/api/ai/workers-ai/…` with `createGatewayFetch()`. More in [AI](/docs/agent/ai).

### Check it worked

- `pnpm everyapp ai list` shows `workers-ai` with its key set, and `pnpm everyapp ai show` says which provider apps get by default.
- `pnpm everyapp status` shows apps that were waiting for it as ready.
